title: Back Sleeping Halved SIDS, But Thousands Still Die
hook: Parents changed one sleep position—and infant deaths fell sharply.
closing: Putting babies on their backs remains a simple step parents can use tonight.
question: Do new parents know this rule?

segments.say: The SIDS rate fell to 0.64 per thousand births. Back sleeping accompanied a drop of more than half.
Before the campaign, 85.4 percent of SIDS cases involved stomach-down placement. That explains why sleep position became the prevention target.
About 3,400 sleep-related infant deaths still occur yearly. The campaign's success did not make safe sleep optional.
